title.narrative: Design Support to the Swedish Gender Equality Agency in Kosovo
Designstöd för program mellan Sveriges och Kosovos jämställdhetsmyndigheter

description.narrative:
Den 27 juni 2022 skickade Jämställdhetsmyndigheten in en ansökan till Sida om att finansiera en designfas för att utveckla ett programförslag om fortsatt kapacitetsutveckling och institutionell förstärkning hos Kosovos jämställdhetsmyndighet, Kosovo Agency for Gender Equality (KAGE).
Designfasen har två spår: Ett för design och planering av ett fullskaligt långsiktigt partnerskap i form av ett treårigt program mellan de båda myndigheterna med sina respektive team.
Det andra spåret handlar om att den svenska myndigheten samtidigt samarbetar med Kosovos Jämställdhetsmyndighet genom konkreta aktiviteter såsom utbyte, workshops eller utbildningar - baserat på tidigare behov från systermyndigheten. Exempel på förbättringar är kunskap om - och genomförande av - gender budgeting, stärkande av kommuners jämställdhetsarbete, intern organisation och kommunikation för den kosovanska myndigheten som samordnande organ.
Designstödfasen ska även omfatta faktainsamling, dialoger med intressenter samt samverkan på managementnivå. Cheferna från respektive myndigheter ska kunna mötas för att diskutera ledningsansvar och departementen kan också inkluderas för ett ökat engagemant för frågorna.
Designstödsfasen föreslås starta den 1 september 2022 och avslutas den 30 september 2023 och budgeten kommer att uppgå till 3 miljoner SEK.
Efter avslutat stöd ska Jämställdhetsmyndigheten presentera två delar:
1) Ett komplett treårigt programförslag med följande komponenter:
- Mål, tillvägagångsätt och metod med organisation av projektet.
- Förändringsteori, resultatsramverk, och uppföljningsindikatorer.
- Identifierade partnerorganisationer, intressenter, och målgrupper.
- Riskanalys och plan för riskreducering.
- Budget med ett inkluderande narrativ för uppföljning.
2) En narrativ reflekterande rapport hur de konkreta aktiviteterna, spår 2, har spelat in till det föreslagna programmet. Parterna ska även beskriva vad de lärt av designfasen och hela processen samt vilka resultat som uppnåtts genom aktiviteterna.

Designstödet innebär ett års arbete med två målsättningar. Den ena är att utveckla ett partnerskap och designa ett program för att långsiktigt stärka jämställdhetsmyndigheten i Kosovo. Den andra handlar om att fortsätta ett pågående arbete med myndighetens stöd till kommuner. I oktober 2023 ska ett nytt program presenteras.

The design support involves a year's work with two objectives. One is to develop a partnership and design a program to strengthen AGE, the Gender Equality Agency, in Kosovo in the long term. The second concerns continuing ongoing work with the authority's support to municipalities. In October 2023, a new program will be presented

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The design phase have had two different periods: The first months consisted with reading reports, policy guidelines and doing analysis of the needs. The second phase was mostly linked to the design of a new program, through workshops and meetings.
During the first months the partners went back to the findings in the evaluation of the earlier cooperation (UM2022/25250/PRIS-2), which was an important baseline and also an important source for Sida to assess the need for continued support. The Swedish financial support during 2015 to 2020, was given directly to the Kosovo Agency for Gender Equality.
As noted before in the appraisal and in earlier statement one of the findings in the evaluation (conducted by FCG in cooperation with Tana and finalized February 24, 2021) was that a long term development should focus more on the existing staff. They should have had more opportunities for capacity development without to many external consultants doing the real work, hands-on. On the positive side, the evaluation showed that the improvement of KAGE as a central agency was clear, with for instance a better cooperation with the municipalities and ministries.
One of the core questions in the second period of the design phase was to identify the coming needs and priorities. Based on already achieved improvements and conclusions from the evaluation, reports and many meetings between the Swedish and Kosvo team some core areas were identified which were presented in the final application for a future collaboration.
These were:
A Strengthened capabilities and accountability of gender mechanism and efficiency of policy instruments.
- Strengthening implementation of gender equality commitments through effective structures and systems - across government at national and local level.
- Developing strategic communication and dissemination on gender equality and better coordination with stakeholders.
B Increased effectiveness of organisational instruments and their application.
- Strengthening the application of gender data and statistics and more efficient monitoring and reporting.
- Strengthening internal organisational capacity in planning, human resources and learning from results.
The partners also found out that they had many different thematic areas that they would like to be integrated in the program. These were for example gender budgeting, gender based - and honor-based violence - integration in systems, internal competence and communication.
Furthermore, to be inspired about the "Swedish model" in building an agency based on trust between the citizens and civil servants, and get ideas on how to improve the connection with different actors and networks, the whole team from KAGE (17 persons) went for a study trip to Sweden. Except from learning about how the Swedish agency coordinates different tasks with other stakeholders, the staff wanted to know more about how the Swedish agency works with human resources. The exchange trip, in September 2023, became very appreciated. During the visit in Sweden the staff gathered in different groups with the Swedish colleagues, to discuss various topics. The partners also sharpened their ideas and had discussions on the identified focus-areas for the future program.
